messages.subject: A few questions about matrices
parts:
I am starting to develop code for MCAR models and need to carry out some matrix manipulations.
The code is pretty crude and could I am sure be optimised, but anyway:
here are a few questions:

I used a kronecker r function call with

kron <- nimbleRcall(function(x = double(2), y = double(2)){}, Rfun = 'kronecker',
returnType = double(2), envir = .GlobalEnv)

Q1: is this valid for a kronecker call in nimble code?
Its not using a nimble function but hoping to use the R function instead, to save on writing my own function.

Q2: the code that calls the function is


Prec[1:K,1:K]~dwish(R[1:K,1:K],K)
Cov[1:K,1:K]<-inverse(Prec[1:K,1:K])
Achol[1:K,1:K]<-chol(Cov[1:K,1:K])
asd[1:kl,1:kl]<-kron(Achol[1:K,1:K],identityMatrix(Nareas))

This appears to work but I am not confident about it.
For example is the Wishart specified correctly? I used the form that BUGS uses with R[,] specifed in the constant list.

also: the chol function: does it return a lower or an upper triangular martrix ?
(its not clear from the documentation)

Q3 the asd is of dimension (K*Nareas x K*Nareas).
I need to premultiply a (K*Nareas x 1) vector by asd.
Is the '*' operator or '%*%' used for matrix multiplication or do I need do element -wise processing.


I can of course send you the code in full as well.

best wishes
Andrew

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about matrices
parts:
Hi Andrew, a few thoughts here:

Q1: that use of nimbleRcall looks good. There is some overhead in
going back and forth from compiled Nimble code to R (in particular we
have to
make copies of inputs and outputs), so that might slow things down a
bunch in some circumstances. To some degree whether it matters
will depend on how intensive the computations within R are and how
long the Kronecker call takes relative to the other stuff you are
doing.
Regardless, starting with nimbleRcall is a good way to prototype things.

Q2: yes, dwish is fine and the rest of the model code looks fine as well.
We have a list of the distribution names for Nimble in Sec. 5.2.4 of
the manual in case anyone is wondering.
But they are essentially the same names as in WinBUGS/JAGS.

chol() returns the upper triangular factor. Good point about the
documentation - we don't seem to say that explicitly,
but we do what R's chol() does. I'll make a note to fix up the docs.

Q3: You can use %*% for matrix-vector multiplication, either in model
code or in the run code of a nimbleFunction.

One thing to watch out for is that the result is a matrix (albeit with
one column).

So if you want to then later treat it as a vector, you'd need to do
something like this in model code:
result[1:m] <- (X[1:m,1:m] %*% y[1:m])[,1]
or in run code you don't need the indexing, but still need to do this
so that result is 1-d not 2-d:
result <- (X%*%y)[,1]
More discussion on this situation for nimbleFunction code is in Sec
11.3.2.5 of the manual.

-chris
